Title: Fort Hill, Patuxent meet for 1A title in clash of defending state champions - CNHI
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
December 6, 2025 by
ANNAPOLIS — Fort Hill’s quest for a state-record fifth consecutive state championship has entered its final chapter.
Just one school stands between the Sentinels and immortality, and it’s a challenging obstacle. Four time-reigning Class 1A champ Fort Hill (9-3) battles defending Class 2A/1A champion Patuxent (9-3) for the 1A crown on Saturday at noon at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium.
Patuxent has established a reputation as a streak-stopper, ending Dunbar’s 51-game winning streak with an 8-6 upset in Annapolis last season.
“It’s going to be a great opportunity,” Fort Hill head coach Zack Alkire said. “It’s two really good programs and two programs that have won state championships in the last calendar year. We’re excited to be able to show the talents that we have against an opponent that is a championship-caliber team.
“We’ve been down there a lot as a coaching staff, as a program, but we have a lot of kids that haven’t gotten to participate in a state championship game. … There’s a lot of excitement for everybody to be able to go out there and show what kind of program we are.”
Fort Hill’s program needs little introduction, having won nine of the past 11 state championships and 11 overall. The Sentinels are third all-time in titles behind Dunbar (13) and Damascus (12).
Since the start of the 2013 season, Fort Hill has a 151-12 record on the field (146-17 officially due to five forfeited games last year). The Sentinels have won 21 straight playoff games under Alkire.
Fort Hill’s 35-0 victory over Northern last year tied the state’s longest consecutive championship streak with its own 2013-16 squad under Todd Appel and Urbana (1998-01).
“No one’s ever done it before, but it’s really just another game,” Alkire said of the possible record. “This is the first championship for this group of kids, and that’s something we need to remember as well. This team hasn’t won a state championship before, so they have to go out and prove it.”

Patuxent, which also won the 2015 Class 2A championship, hails from the small town of Lusby in Calvert County.
The Panthers have eyed a potential matchup with Fort Hill since the Southern Maryland squad was reclassified to Class 1A this year.
“As soon as we went to 1A, it was, Fort Hill’s our new Dunbar, so we have to figure out how to match their level,” Patuxent head coach Steve Crounse said. “They execute at such a high level. I really enjoy watching them because of how they execute. It’s going to be a tall task for us.”
Fort Hill and Patuxent have met three times previously, with the Sentinels holding a 2-1 edge.
Fort Hill won 35-3 in 1998 and 8-0 in 2002, and the Panthers were victorious 20-8 in ‘01.
SMAC Supremacy
Crounse’s Panthers knocked out Fort Hill’s rival Allegany, 42-0, in the state quarterfinals and rebuffed an upset bid from Boonsboro in a 35-27 semifinal victory.
Patuxent’s region final rout of Washington, 48-0, was the team’s first game against a Class 1A opponent all season.
The Panthers are a member of the highly-respected Southern Maryland Athletic Conference, a league that boasts four teams playing for state championships this week.
At least two SMAC squads have competed for state titles in each of the past five seasons.
How deep is the league? SMAC champion Calvert, which Patuxent defeated 21-14 in Week 8, is not one of those four programs that have advanced to Annapolis.
Fort Hill has faced Western Maryland opposition in all four of its championship games during the streak, defeating Mountain Ridge thrice from 2021-23 before its victory over Northern in last year’s final.
The Sentinels have an opportunity to prove their worth against one of the state’s most respected programs over the last decade.
Big Red Redemption
The Panthers could be running into a buzzsaw in the form of a Fort Hill team that has dominated its past seven opponents.

The Sentinels fell to Bridgeport, 49-14, in Week 5 to start 2-3 for the first time since 2001 but have rallied with seven romps in a row by a margin of 398-56 (56.9-8.0 average) — the latest a 56-19 rout of Perryville in the state semifinals.
“Nobody likes to lose, and the kids do take it to heart,” Alkire said. “They had every opportunity to lay down and let their season kind of fade away. But they’re a resilient group of kids that have that championship mentality, and they knew what they wanted, they knew what their goals were and they knew that they were going to get better.
“They had patience with us, we had patience with them and it’s all kind of worked out for us here in the last couple weeks.”
Chasing History
Not only is Fort Hill chasing history as a team. Two individuals, fullback Braelyn Younger and quarterback Noah House, can etch their names in the record books with strong performances Saturday.
Younger racked up 276 yards and four touchdowns last week against Perryville, becoming the sixth Fort Hill player to score 30 touchdowns and third to eclipse 2,000 yards in one season.
For the year, the fullback has 182 carries for 2,105 yards and 31 total touchdowns. He has 2,411 all-purpose yards to lead the area.
Younger currently sits third in area history in single-season rushing behind only Fort Hill’s Jabril Daniels (2,276, 2024) and Josh Page (2,274, 1996).
Daniels and Allegany’s Karson Robinette (2017) share the city single-season touchdown record of 34, a feat Daniels achieved twice (‘23, ‘24).
Frankfort’s Travis Lynch holds the area record with 35 (1997).
“Just watching the Younger kid, I mean, he’s going to be the best back that we would have faced all year,” Crounse said, “and actually, for me, probably (one of the best) in the 33 years I’ve been coaching. He’s pretty good. He runs hard for sure.”

House is just the sixth Fort Hill passer to top 1,000 yards in a campaign. The senior enters the championship game with 1,181 yards and 13 touchdowns to just one interception.
House is nearing school-record marks set by Gavin Palumbo, who threw for 1,274 yards and 15 touchdowns in 1993.
Scouting Patuxent
Patuxent has a pass-first spread offense, with 61% of its total offense coming through the air.
Senior wideout Evan Jones, who holds offers from Maryland and Virginia Tech, is the Panthers’ top offensive threat with 754 yards and 11 touchdowns on 67 receptions.
Jones has seen his workload in the backfield increase after Patuxent’s feature back, Antoine Wilkins, was lost for the season to a collarbone injury.
Jones had 16 carries for 80 yards and two scores against Boonsboro and has 402 yards and seven touchdowns on the ground for the season.
“He’s their guy,” Alkire said. “They want to get him the ball any way they can. If they feel that they can get him the ball in the backfield, that’s what they’re going to do. If they feel that they can get the ball to him better out as a receiver, that’s what they’re going to do.”
Patuxent freshman quarterback Brayden Watson has been highly efficient, completing 73% of his passes for 2,349 yards and 28 touchdowns to six interceptions.
Another receiver, Peyton Johnson (599 yards, eight touchdowns), has an offer from Division 2 West Liberty.
“I think we need to get a lot of pressure on the quarterback,” Alkire said. “Making him make quicker decisions than what he might be used to. Making him get the ball out a little bit earlier than what he’s used to try to disrupt him a little bit. I think that’s the biggest key for us defensively.”
Fort Hill’s Christian Riley and Dylan Leatherman lead the team with 4.5 sacks each.
The Sentinels’ defense had no interceptions during the regular season, but it has seven in the postseason from six players, including five pick-sixes in the past two weeks.
Fort Hill’s opponents are completing just 34% of their passes (45 for 134).

Title: Inside Maryland High School Football: A Wild Finish in Cumberland and More Forfeits
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6
Rise and Reclaim is alive and well in Cumberland, Maryland, as the Fort Hillfootballteam continued its redemption tour with a heart-stopping 43-42 victory over Bridgeport (W.Va.) on Friday.

## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
The game featured four touchdowns in the final 7:36, a successful two-point conversion in the closing minute, and a missed field goal on the final play in one of the most dramatic finishes this season.
The victory marked the second straight week Fort Hill avenged a 2025 loss as it continues its quest to reclaim its position as the state’s top 1A program. Fort Hill won four straight state championships before falling in last year’s state final, prompting the “Rise and Reclaim” motto for 2026. Fort Hill took a big step in that direction last week with a 35-21 victory over Hollidaysburg (Pa.). But Bridgeport was a different kind of monster.
Last year, Bridgeport handed Fort Hill a 49-14 thrashing in West Virginia, Fort Hill’s most lopsided regular-season loss since 2012. Friday’s rematch at Greenway Avenue Stadium carried historical significance, marking Bridgeport’s first game outside West Virginia after 1,098 consecutive in-state contests dating to 1921. The Sentinels again found themselves in trouble Friday, falling behind 21-7 before Bridgeport scored on a 70-yard play in the closing seconds of the second quarter to take a 28-14 halftime lead.
Fort Hill rallied to tie the game at 28 in the third quarter, setting up a wild finish.
Bridgeport took a 35-28 lead with 7:36 remaining, but Brady O’Neal answered 62 seconds later with a 78-yard touchdown pass to Carson Bender. Bridgeport again surged ahead, 42-35, before a three-minute Fort Hill drive was capped by Neek Taylor’s 7-yard scoring run, making it 42-41. There was no hesitation about going for two.
“When we started the next drive [down 42-35], everyone knew we’d be going for two,” Fort Hill coach Zach Alkire said.
After Bridgeport burned a timeout, Fort Hill called a quick pitch to the left. The wing got just enough of a block to give Taylor the room he needed to barely cross the goal line, putting Fort Hill ahead 43-42 with 51 seconds remaining.

## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
Bridgeport quickly moved into field-goal range, aided by a defensive pass-interference penalty. An encroachment penalty moved the final attempt from 44 to 39 yards, but the kick had the distance and sailed just wide right, sending Fort Hill to 5-0.
“The sideline went nuts,” Alkire said. “Kids running off the field, hugging. There was a lot of excitement, and we needed that.”

## **100 Wins, 46 Years in the Making**
Washington defeated Nandua (Va.), 20-10, in a contest that could easily be overlooked among the more than 100 games played by Maryland high schools this past weekend.
For Washington, however, it was anything but ordinary. The victory marked the program’s 100th varsity win — a milestone 46 years in the making.
Washington launched its first varsity football team in 1980 and lost its debut 42-0 to James M. Bennett. That proved to be a sign of things to come.
Except for the COVID-19 pandemic season in 2020, Washington has put a varsity team on the field every year since 1980. During that time, Washington has had only two winning seasons: 7-4 in 1989 and 8-5 in 2003. Yet the program has persevered despite finishing at or near the bottom of the Bayside standings for much of its history.
Perhaps the times are changing for this tiny school, which has about 600 students in grades 8-12.
Alec Meintzer inherited the program in 2023 while it was mired in an 18-game losing streak. That streak eventually reached 38 games before Washington broke through with a 16-6 victory over North East-Cecil last season. The win sparked something bigger: Washington finished 5-5, its first non-losing season since 2003.
Meintzer stepped down after the season, and Tremont White has taken over. This year’s team is officially 2-2, as the MPSSAA ruled that a scheduled season opener at Northampton (Va.) was a no-contest since the game was not played.
Now Washington has a chance to reach 3-2 for the first time since 1998 when it faces Arcadia (Va.) on Friday. The Jaguars defeated Arcadia, 36-16, last season.

## **Forfeits, No-Contests Becoming an Unwanted Trend**
The Maryland high school football season has reached the halfway point, and an unusual number of games have disappeared from the schedule because of forfeits, no-contests, or teams dropping games altogether.
The latest came this past weekend in Prince George’s County. According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line after the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests. The two teams will also play their remaining games this season on Saturdays.
According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line following the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests.
It is the latest in a growing list of unusual circumstances that have taken games off the schedule this season.
North Point and Westlake forfeited their season openers in Charles County because of what was termed out-of-season contact violations. Maryland School for the Deaf received a forfeit victory when its scheduled opponent disbanded the week of the game. Annapolis Area Christian has forfeited two games because of a lack of healthy players.
Weather has also played a role. Northampton (Va.) canceled its scheduled game at Washington because of what was described as “extreme heat,” while weather-related no-contests cost Flowers and Wise games from their schedules.
The situation has been particularly interesting at Edmondson-Westside. Through five weeks, the team has played only two games. One scheduled game was a forfeit, and two others were never played after Hancock and Benjamin Franklin dropped their football programs before the season.
This past weekend, Sidwell Friends, which rejoined the Mid-Atlantic Conference this season, forfeited its league opener at St. James on Saturday, citing not enough healthy players.
Meanwhile, Central Maryland Christian, down to 18 players, has reduced its regular-season schedule to four games.
While the reasons are varied, the result is the same: fewer opportunities for players to compete and an increasingly unpredictable high school football schedule.

## **Crofton Remains Unbeaten**
Crofton was featured early this season after what was then considered an upset victory over Old Mill.
Now, the Wildcats have established themselves as the team to beat in Anne Arundel County. Crofton is the county’s lone 5-0 team and one of just 21 undefeated teams remaining in the MPSSAA.
Dominic Jackson delivered the latest heroics, scoring on a 3-yard run to lift Crofton to a 20-17 overtime victory over Chesapeake-AA.
The teams tied at 14 after regulation. Gary Windsor gave Chesapeake-AA a 17-14 lead in the first overtime with a 27-yard field goal, but Crofton answered with a touchdown to complete the comeback and remain unbeaten.

## **Got Your Number**
Northwestern-PG edged Bladensburg, 22-20, over the weekend, marking the third consecutive year the Wildcats have beaten the Mustangs.
While the streak is notable, it is even more remarkable that Bladensburg is the only team Northwestern-PG has beaten since 2019.
Since midseason 2019, Northwestern-PG is 4-2 against Bladensburg but 0-53 against all other opponents. The Wildcats’ last victory over anyone other than Bladensburg came on Oct. 12, 2019, when Northwestern-PG thrashed DuVal, 47-6.

by Sydney Skidmore and Dean Hensley
Wed, August 5, 2026 at 6:12 AM
Updated Wed, August 5, 2026 at 5:10 PM
OCT. 21, 2025 - Congressman Chuck Edwards. (Photo credit: WLOS Staff)
HENDERSONVILLE, N.C. (WLOS) — United States Congressman Chuck Edwards, who represents North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, has withdrawn from his re-election campaign.
Video 3
The news was posted to his Facebook page just before 5 a.m. on Aug. 5.
Edwards said he plans to complete his term, but cites much prayer and reflection in making the difficult decision. This announcement comes after the U.S. House Committee on Ethics recommended a censure, following allegations of sexual misconduct with some of his staffers.
Withdrawal form signed by Edwards PDF preview
View PDF
That recommendation stems from the committee concluding in a new report that there is substantial reason to believe he violated House rules, creating a hostile workplace. The report alleges Edwards gave two female staffers a surplus of gifts– including jewelry totaling over $1,000, designer purses, guns, flowers, vacations and "one-on-one" dinners.
Edwards also recently announced that he and his wife had sold all of their McDonald'srestaurants in western North Carolina.
A spokesperson with Edwards' campaign says the committee's report clears him of allegations of sexual activity or explicitly propositioning staff.
**REP. CHUCK EDWARDS FACES POLITICAL FALLOUT AFTER HOUSE ETHICS REPORT RECOMMENDS CENSURE**
Edwards won the May Primary for the Republican candidate for North Carolina District 11. With his withdrawal, the local Republican party will now choose a replacement candidate to run on the GOP ticket.
As for his Democratic nominee, Jamie Ager is still in the race, and he issued this statement about Edwards' withdrawal:

> This campaign has never been about any one person. It’s always been about Western North Carolina and our communities getting the leadership and representation we deserve. That has not changed. For too long, we’ve been forgotten by politicians who sell us a false bill of goods, then go to Congress to treat D.C. as their personal playground while we get left behind. My heart goes out to the young women who took these roles to serve our community. No matter who we face in November, I’m confident we can win this race and deliver what I’ve been talking about since day one: Hurricane Helene recovery, lower costs, and an end to the corruption in Washington.

## Indictment and conviction
On January 13, 2011, Edwards was released from prison and served the remainder of his sentence at a halfway house.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-69) His sentence ended on July 6, 2011[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-70) and he began three years of probation. He entered into home confinement at his daughter's Denham Springs, Louisiana home through the supervision of a halfway house, on January 13, 2011. Following that, Edwards was placed on probation.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-Washington_Post-72) On February 7, 2013, Edwards was granted early release from probation due to good behavior.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-73) His wife Trina made the announcement on her Facebook page.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-75)
In a poll taken in October 2011, months after he had been released from prison, 30 percent of respondents named Edwards the state's best governor since 1980.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-76)

## 2014 Congressional election
[edit]
In February 2014, Edwards announced that he was contemplating running in the 2014 election to represent [Louisiana's 6th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana's_6th_congressional_district "Louisiana's 6th congressional district") in the U.S. House of Representatives, which is centered on the state capital of Baton Rouge. With U.S. Representative Bill Cassidy exiting the seat to run for the Senate, Edwards said of the solidly Republican district: "I'm the only hope the Democrats have here."[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-77) He formally declared his candidacy at a March 17 meeting of the Press Club of Baton Rouge, saying, "I want you to know, I'm going to give it every effort."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-78) If no candidate wins a majority of the vote, a runoff would be held on December 6, 2014, between the top two candidates. Two other Democrats, a Libertarian and nine Republicans, most notably Garret Graves, a former aide to Governor Bobby Jindal, State Senator Dan Claitor, businessman Paul Dietzel II, and State Representative Lenar Whitney, also sought the seat.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-79)

## 2014 Congressional election
After Edwards' announcement, Cassidy told KEEL radio news in Shreveport that he doubted that Edwards "has a chance. It's a conservative district, and he's obviously not a conservative. But it kind of shows, I think, to a certain extent that the Democratic bench is weak."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-80) Louisiana political writer John Maginnis said that Edwards was "likely to make the runoff" because of his name recognition, but "I don't see how he could win in a strong GOP-performance district like the 6th. But it should be entertaining." State pollster Elliott Stonecipher said that "the most basic math of the Edwards race yields an 'it is not impossible' answer" and former governor Buddy Roemer said that while it is unlikely, "yes, [Edwards] can win".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-laststand-5)
An April 2014 article in _Politico_ that discussed his chances noted that he was "still sharp as a razor" and "in remarkably vigorous health".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-laststand-5) He pronounced himself "disappointed" with President Obama for "sitting" on the Keystone Pipeline and listed his campaign priorities as "Building support for a high-speed rail system between Baton Rouge and New Orleans and emphasizing the good aspects of Obamacare, while doing what I can to change or amend the provisions that I think are onerous."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-laststand-5) He said that he would have voted against the Affordable Care Act, but criticized Governor Jindal for not accepting the Medicaid expansion. If elected, he hoped to serve on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, to spur the construction of elevated roadways in the state.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-81)

## 2014 Congressional election
A September 2014 survey of statewide Louisiana voters by Public Policy Polling found that 40% had a favourable opinion of Edwards, 44% did not and 17% were unsure. Asked whether they would rather have Edwards as governor than incumbent Republican governor Bobby Jindal, 47% said they would prefer Edwards, 43% preferred Jindal and 10% were not sure.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-82)
Edwards finished first in every poll taken of the race, though only with a plurality. Runoff polls showed him losing to all of his Republican opponents. An article in _The Times-Picayune_ in late October 2014 noted that he had run a vigorous, serious campaign and noted that, as previously, analysts were split on whether he could actually win. David Wasserman of _The Cook Political Report_ said that for Edwards, "mathematically, victory is something close to impossibility." Conversely, a spokesman for Republican opponent Lenar Whitney and political analyst Michael Beychok both said that he had a chance to win and Republican candidate Garret Graves said "There's no one alive anymore in this state that has the experience or, quite frankly, the tactics (of) Edwin Edwards." Edwards was expected to make the runoff, with his chances dependent on which Republican joins him, with several analysts saying that Edwards' best chance would come if Whitney, the most conservative Republican running, does so. Edwards' strategy was to appeal to black and Cajun voters and conservative Democrats, also campaigning on college campuses to appeal to younger voters. Columnist Bob Mann predicted that if Edwards made the runoff, the media would decry Louisiana voters' toleration for corruption when, "in truth (Edwards) never really had a chance to win."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-83)

## 2014 Congressional election
As expected, Edwards as the principal Democratic candidate led the 2014 primary field for Congress with 77,862 votes (30.1 percent), winning every parish in the district.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-84) He then faced the Republican runner-up, Garret Graves, in the December 6 runoff election. Graves had received 70,706 "jungle primary" votes (27.4 percent). Losing Republican candidates were Paul Dietzel II, with 35,013 votes (13.6 percent), state Senator Dan Claitor with 26,520 (10.3 percent), and state Representative Lenar Whitney with 19,146 votes (7.4 percent).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-85) Edwards lost to Graves by a 62–38 percent margin in the runoff. It was only the second loss of his political career.
However, in 2024, the election data analysis website Split Ticket found that Edwards had overperformed the Democratic baseline in the district with a Wins above replacement (WAR) score of D+24.5.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-:0-86)

## Indictment and conviction
On January 13, 2011, Edwards was released from prison and served the remainder of his sentence at a halfway house.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-69) His sentence ended on July 6, 2011[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-70) and he began three years of probation. He entered into home confinement at his daughter's Denham Springs, Louisiana home through the supervision of a halfway house, on January 13, 2011. Following that, Edwards was placed on probation.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-Washington_Post-72) On February 7, 2013, Edwards was granted early release from probation due to good behavior.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-73) His wife Trina made the announcement on her Facebook page.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-75)
In a poll taken in October 2011, months after he had been released from prison, 30 percent of respondents named Edwards the state's best governor since 1980.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-76)
texts.31:
## 2014 Congressional election
[edit]
In February 2014, Edwards announced that he was contemplating running in the 2014 election to represent [Louisiana's 6th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana's_6th_congressional_district "Louisiana's 6th congressional district") in the U.S. House of Representatives, which is centered on the state capital of Baton Rouge. With U.S. Representative Bill Cassidy exiting the seat to run for the Senate, Edwards said of the solidly Republican district: "I'm the only hope the Democrats have here."[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-77) He formally declared his candidacy at a March 17 meeting of the Press Club of Baton Rouge, saying, "I want you to know, I'm going to give it every effort."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-78) If no candidate wins a majority of the vote, a runoff would be held on December 6, 2014, between the top two candidates. Two other Democrats, a Libertarian and nine Republicans, most notably Garret Graves, a former aide to Governor Bobby Jindal, State Senator Dan Claitor, businessman Paul Dietzel II, and State Representative Lenar Whitney, also sought the seat.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-79)
texts.32:
## 2014 Congressional election
After Edwards' announcement, Cassidy told KEEL radio news in Shreveport that he doubted that Edwards "has a chance. It's a conservative district, and he's obviously not a conservative. But it kind of shows, I think, to a certain extent that the Democratic bench is weak."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-80) Louisiana political writer John Maginnis said that Edwards was "likely to make the runoff" because of his name recognition, but "I don't see how he could win in a strong GOP-performance district like the 6th. But it should be entertaining." State pollster Elliott Stonecipher said that "the most basic math of the Edwards race yields an 'it is not impossible' answer" and former governor Buddy Roemer said that while it is unlikely, "yes, [Edwards] can win".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-laststand-5)
An April 2014 article in _Politico_ that discussed his chances noted that he was "still sharp as a razor" and "in remarkably vigorous health".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-laststand-5) He pronounced himself "disappointed" with President Obama for "sitting" on the Keystone Pipeline and listed his campaign priorities as "Building support for a high-speed rail system between Baton Rouge and New Orleans and emphasizing the good aspects of Obamacare, while doing what I can to change or amend the provisions that I think are onerous."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-laststand-5) He said that he would have voted against the Affordable Care Act, but criticized Governor Jindal for not accepting the Medicaid expansion. If elected, he hoped to serve on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, to spur the construction of elevated roadways in the state.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-81)
texts.33:
## 2014 Congressional election
A September 2014 survey of statewide Louisiana voters by Public Policy Polling found that 40% had a favourable opinion of Edwards, 44% did not and 17% were unsure. Asked whether they would rather have Edwards as governor than incumbent Republican governor Bobby Jindal, 47% said they would prefer Edwards, 43% preferred Jindal and 10% were not sure.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-82)
Edwards finished first in every poll taken of the race, though only with a plurality. Runoff polls showed him losing to all of his Republican opponents. An article in _The Times-Picayune_ in late October 2014 noted that he had run a vigorous, serious campaign and noted that, as previously, analysts were split on whether he could actually win. David Wasserman of _The Cook Political Report_ said that for Edwards, "mathematically, victory is something close to impossibility." Conversely, a spokesman for Republican opponent Lenar Whitney and political analyst Michael Beychok both said that he had a chance to win and Republican candidate Garret Graves said "There's no one alive anymore in this state that has the experience or, quite frankly, the tactics (of) Edwin Edwards." Edwards was expected to make the runoff, with his chances dependent on which Republican joins him, with several analysts saying that Edwards' best chance would come if Whitney, the most conservative Republican running, does so. Edwards' strategy was to appeal to black and Cajun voters and conservative Democrats, also campaigning on college campuses to appeal to younger voters. Columnist Bob Mann predicted that if Edwards made the runoff, the media would decry Louisiana voters' toleration for corruption when, "in truth (Edwards) never really had a chance to win."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-83)
texts.34:
## 2014 Congressional election
As expected, Edwards as the principal Democratic candidate led the 2014 primary field for Congress with 77,862 votes (30.1 percent), winning every parish in the district.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-84) He then faced the Republican runner-up, Garret Graves, in the December 6 runoff election. Graves had received 70,706 "jungle primary" votes (27.4 percent). Losing Republican candidates were Paul Dietzel II, with 35,013 votes (13.6 percent), state Senator Dan Claitor with 26,520 (10.3 percent), and state Representative Lenar Whitney with 19,146 votes (7.4 percent).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-85) Edwards lost to Graves by a 62–38 percent margin in the runoff. It was only the second loss of his political career.
However, in 2024, the election data analysis website Split Ticket found that Edwards had overperformed the Democratic baseline in the district with a Wins above replacement (WAR) score of D+24.5.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-:0-86)

Conversely, a spokesman for Republican opponent Lenar Whitney and political analyst Michael Beychok both said that he had a chance to win and Republican candidate Garret Graves said "There's no one alive anymore in this state that has the experience or, quite frankly, the tactics (of) Edwin Edwards." Edwards was expected to make the runoff, with his chances dependent on which Republican joins him, with several analysts saying that Edwards' best chance would come if Whitney, the most conservative Republican running, does so. Edwards' strategy was to appeal to black and Cajun voters and conservative Democrats, also campaigning on college campuses to appeal to younger voters. Columnist Bob Mann predicted that if Edwards made the runoff, the media would decry Louisiana voters' toleration for corruption when, "in truth (Edwards) never really had a chance to win."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-83)

## 2014 Congressional election
As expected, Edwards as the principal Democratic candidate led the 2014 primary field for Congress with 77,862 votes (30.1 percent), winning every parish in the district.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-84) He then faced the Republican runner-up, Garret Graves, in the December 6 runoff election. Graves had received 70,706 "jungle primary" votes (27.4 percent). Losing Republican candidates were Paul Dietzel II, with 35,013 votes (13.6 percent), state Senator Dan Claitor with 26,520 (10.3 percent), and state Representative Lenar Whitney with 19,146 votes (7.4 percent).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-85) Edwards lost to Graves by a 62–38 percent margin in the runoff. It was only the second loss of his political career.
However, in 2024, the election data analysis website Split Ticket found that Edwards had overperformed the Democratic baseline in the district with a Wins above replacement (WAR) score of D+24.5.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Edwards#cite_note-:0-86)

Title: Inside Maryland High School Football: A Wild Finish in Cumberland and More Forfeits
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6
Rise and Reclaim is alive and well in Cumberland, Maryland, as the Fort Hillfootballteam continued its redemption tour with a heart-stopping 43-42 victory over Bridgeport (W.Va.) on Friday.

## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
The game featured four touchdowns in the final 7:36, a successful two-point conversion in the closing minute, and a missed field goal on the final play in one of the most dramatic finishes this season.
The victory marked the second straight week Fort Hill avenged a 2025 loss as it continues its quest to reclaim its position as the state’s top 1A program. Fort Hill won four straight state championships before falling in last year’s state final, prompting the “Rise and Reclaim” motto for 2026. Fort Hill took a big step in that direction last week with a 35-21 victory over Hollidaysburg (Pa.). But Bridgeport was a different kind of monster.
Last year, Bridgeport handed Fort Hill a 49-14 thrashing in West Virginia, Fort Hill’s most lopsided regular-season loss since 2012. Friday’s rematch at Greenway Avenue Stadium carried historical significance, marking Bridgeport’s first game outside West Virginia after 1,098 consecutive in-state contests dating to 1921. The Sentinels again found themselves in trouble Friday, falling behind 21-7 before Bridgeport scored on a 70-yard play in the closing seconds of the second quarter to take a 28-14 halftime lead.
Fort Hill rallied to tie the game at 28 in the third quarter, setting up a wild finish.
Bridgeport took a 35-28 lead with 7:36 remaining, but Brady O’Neal answered 62 seconds later with a 78-yard touchdown pass to Carson Bender. Bridgeport again surged ahead, 42-35, before a three-minute Fort Hill drive was capped by Neek Taylor’s 7-yard scoring run, making it 42-41. There was no hesitation about going for two.
“When we started the next drive [down 42-35], everyone knew we’d be going for two,” Fort Hill coach Zach Alkire said.
After Bridgeport burned a timeout, Fort Hill called a quick pitch to the left. The wing got just enough of a block to give Taylor the room he needed to barely cross the goal line, putting Fort Hill ahead 43-42 with 51 seconds remaining.

## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
Bridgeport quickly moved into field-goal range, aided by a defensive pass-interference penalty. An encroachment penalty moved the final attempt from 44 to 39 yards, but the kick had the distance and sailed just wide right, sending Fort Hill to 5-0.
“The sideline went nuts,” Alkire said. “Kids running off the field, hugging. There was a lot of excitement, and we needed that.”

## **100 Wins, 46 Years in the Making**
Washington defeated Nandua (Va.), 20-10, in a contest that could easily be overlooked among the more than 100 games played by Maryland high schools this past weekend.
For Washington, however, it was anything but ordinary. The victory marked the program’s 100th varsity win — a milestone 46 years in the making.
Washington launched its first varsity football team in 1980 and lost its debut 42-0 to James M. Bennett. That proved to be a sign of things to come.
Except for the COVID-19 pandemic season in 2020, Washington has put a varsity team on the field every year since 1980. During that time, Washington has had only two winning seasons: 7-4 in 1989 and 8-5 in 2003. Yet the program has persevered despite finishing at or near the bottom of the Bayside standings for much of its history.
Perhaps the times are changing for this tiny school, which has about 600 students in grades 8-12.
Alec Meintzer inherited the program in 2023 while it was mired in an 18-game losing streak. That streak eventually reached 38 games before Washington broke through with a 16-6 victory over North East-Cecil last season. The win sparked something bigger: Washington finished 5-5, its first non-losing season since 2003.
Meintzer stepped down after the season, and Tremont White has taken over. This year’s team is officially 2-2, as the MPSSAA ruled that a scheduled season opener at Northampton (Va.) was a no-contest since the game was not played.
Now Washington has a chance to reach 3-2 for the first time since 1998 when it faces Arcadia (Va.) on Friday. The Jaguars defeated Arcadia, 36-16, last season.

## **Forfeits, No-Contests Becoming an Unwanted Trend**
The Maryland high school football season has reached the halfway point, and an unusual number of games have disappeared from the schedule because of forfeits, no-contests, or teams dropping games altogether.
The latest came this past weekend in Prince George’s County. According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line after the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests. The two teams will also play their remaining games this season on Saturdays.
According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line following the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests.
It is the latest in a growing list of unusual circumstances that have taken games off the schedule this season.
North Point and Westlake forfeited their season openers in Charles County because of what was termed out-of-season contact violations. Maryland School for the Deaf received a forfeit victory when its scheduled opponent disbanded the week of the game. Annapolis Area Christian has forfeited two games because of a lack of healthy players.
Weather has also played a role. Northampton (Va.) canceled its scheduled game at Washington because of what was described as “extreme heat,” while weather-related no-contests cost Flowers and Wise games from their schedules.
The situation has been particularly interesting at Edmondson-Westside. Through five weeks, the team has played only two games. One scheduled game was a forfeit, and two others were never played after Hancock and Benjamin Franklin dropped their football programs before the season.
This past weekend, Sidwell Friends, which rejoined the Mid-Atlantic Conference this season, forfeited its league opener at St. James on Saturday, citing not enough healthy players.
Meanwhile, Central Maryland Christian, down to 18 players, has reduced its regular-season schedule to four games.
While the reasons are varied, the result is the same: fewer opportunities for players to compete and an increasingly unpredictable high school football schedule.

## **Crofton Remains Unbeaten**
Crofton was featured early this season after what was then considered an upset victory over Old Mill.
Now, the Wildcats have established themselves as the team to beat in Anne Arundel County. Crofton is the county’s lone 5-0 team and one of just 21 undefeated teams remaining in the MPSSAA.
Dominic Jackson delivered the latest heroics, scoring on a 3-yard run to lift Crofton to a 20-17 overtime victory over Chesapeake-AA.
The teams tied at 14 after regulation. Gary Windsor gave Chesapeake-AA a 17-14 lead in the first overtime with a 27-yard field goal, but Crofton answered with a touchdown to complete the comeback and remain unbeaten.

## **Got Your Number**
Northwestern-PG edged Bladensburg, 22-20, over the weekend, marking the third consecutive year the Wildcats have beaten the Mustangs.
While the streak is notable, it is even more remarkable that Bladensburg is the only team Northwestern-PG has beaten since 2019.
Since midseason 2019, Northwestern-PG is 4-2 against Bladensburg but 0-53 against all other opponents. The Wildcats’ last victory over anyone other than Bladensburg came on Oct. 12, 2019, when Northwestern-PG thrashed DuVal, 47-6.

CUMBERLAND — Even after putting up a combined 91 points in the last two weeks, all wasn't perfect for Fort Hill.
Between the Sentinels' two games in Washington County, they committed more than 40 penalties.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Fort Hill has a chance to start fresh when it returns to Greenway Avenue Stadium for the annual Homecoming game against city rival Allegany on Saturday at 12:30 p.m.

# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
The Sentinels, who wrapped up the top seed in the Class 1A West Region playoffs with last week's 49-14 thrashing over Smithsburg, haven't played at Greenway since Oct. 2.
Since their come-from-behind, 43-42 win over West Virginia power Bridgeport, the Sentinels have played at Mountain Ridge, North Hagerstown and Smithsburg.
Senior running back/linebacker Carson Bender admitted that the Sentinels had played a bit out of their element the past two weeks and a return to Greenway for Homecoming will be welcomed.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
"It's definitely mental stuff," Bender said after the win over Smithsburg. "We gotta be able to keep our cool. You know, Washington County being there for two weeks now, obviously the penalties ramped up there.
"We gotta clean it up. I think being back at home and being in our element next week and throughout the playoffs, that'll help us out a lot."
No. 1 Fort Hill (8-0) and No. 4 Allegany (5-3) will meet for the 106th time. The Sentinels have won 22 straight over the Campers and lead the all-time series 69-32-4.
Fort Hill won last year's game 57-13, setting records for the largest margin of victory and most points in series history.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Braelyn Younger also rushed for a record 203 yards and equalled the all-time touchdown mark with five scores.
"They're playing each other sometimes since five or six years old up through the Pop Warner stages and JV levels," Fort Hill coach Zack Alkire said. "There's lots of familiarity between the kids and what each team can do.
"Both sides look forward to it, both players and coaches, and this year's no different. It's obviously one of the games we circle on the calendar. The kids are pretty amped up for it."
Sophomore Levi House will make his third consecutive start at quarterback in place of Brady O'Neal.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement

# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
House moved over to signal-caller from the tight end spot starting with the North Hagerstown game. In that game, House threw just one incompletion as the Sentinels ran for 369 yards.
But in last week's matchup with Smithsburg, the Sentinels weren't able to pop off as many explosive runs, forcing House to resort to his arm more often.
House gave the Leopards' defense fits all night, completing 7 of 10 passes for 110 yards while adding 60 yards with his feet.
"He completed a lot of those passes," Alkire said. "He made a lot of good decisions. He made a couple other decisions to run the ball instead of throwing the ball. So (we're) really happy with Levi's progress at the quarterback position and look forward to seeing how he can open things up a little bit on Saturday."
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
The Sentinels still grounded 269 yards on the Leopards. Fort Hill's longest run was a 45-yard touchdown by Channing Logsdon in the first quarter. Its second-biggest run was a 20-yarder by House.
Ground yards won't be easy to come by against an Allegany team that's given up an average of 15.2 points during its five-game win streak.
Bender leads the Sentinels with 879 yards rushing and has 13 touchdowns. He also led the team with 96 yards last week.
Neek Taylor has contributed 730 yards and 15 touchdowns. Logsdon (345 yards) and Isaiah Welsh (262 yards) have also been vital parts of Fort Hill's ground game.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Defensively, Fort Hill has allowed just 98 points overall for an average of 12.3 per game.
"We gotta come off the football first and foremost," Alkire said. "Our offensive line needs to be able to track people off the ball without holding and blocking in the back. We need to cut down on the penalties from the previous two weeks and hold onto the football.

# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
"We're gonna have to play really aggressive defense. We're gonna have to defend the pass when needed to, get pressure on the quarterback, make sure all of our gaps are filled and be aggressive running towards the football."
Since there are only seven teams in the West Region, Fort Hill will receive a first-round bye.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
As it stands now, Allegany is the No. 4 seed and will meet No. 5 Southern in the quarterfinals.
A Campers win in that game would set up a rematch between the city rivals in the region semifinals.
Fort Hill and Allegany played once last season, but met twice in 2024. The Sentinels won both games by an 87-0 margin on their way to an 11th state title.
"Homecoming's an important game for the community for both sides," Alkire said. "It's a game that you obviously wanna win. But the reality of it is that the playoffs are coming and a win would really give you a lot of momentum going into the playoffs."

Patuxent High School defensive lineman Jahkiye Dixon returns a fumble 23 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter of Dec. 13 1A state championship game against Fort Hill at the Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis.

# Patuxent wins 1A football championship
But that advantage was long forgotten in the waning seconds of the fourth quarter as the Panthers rallied for an improbable 35-28 victory to end the Sentinels’ four-year reign as 1A state champions.
“That was the greatest game that I’ve ever been a part of,” Patuxent coach Steve Crounse said after the Panthers recorded their second straight state title and third overall. “This group of young teenagers has so much resiliency. When we got that touchdown right before halftime, you could just feel their confidence growing.”
Fort Hill (9-4) owned a 21-7 lead at the end of the first quarter and then pushed the advantage to 28-7 with 2:23 remaining in the first half when quarterback Noah House connected with James Powell-Morris on a 47-yard touchdown strike on the Sentinels’ only play of that possession. Faced with a daunting task against the four-time reigning champs, Patuxent countered with a pivotal late score before the intermission.
Patuxent closed out the first half by marching 55 yards in nine plays, primarily on runs from Evan Jones. Then on the final play of the first half, Watson connected with Coen Boorstein on a 24-yard touchdown strike that trimmed the Sentinels’ lead to 28-14 heading into the locker room. But what was once a comfortable advantage would evaporate over the next 12 minutes.
“I just saw Coen make a good break on the ball and got it out to him and he brought it in,” Watson said. “I know last year they had a lot of seniors, but we just came in and believed in each other and our coaches.”
Fort Hill opened the third quarter with a methodical, 12-play drive that lasted over six minutes but failed to yield any points and that served to bolster the Panthers’ resolve. On its second play of the second half, Watson connected with Peyton Johnson on a 79-yard scoring strike to trim the gap to 28-21, then Jones brought the Panthers even on a 38-yard run.

# Patuxent wins 1A football championship
In a game initially highlighted by big offensive plays, it was the Panthers’ defense that provided the biggest one of all. On the Sentinels’ ensuing possession, Patuxent’s John Edwards sacked House and jarred the ball loose from the Fort Hill quarterback and Jahkiye Dixon snared the ball in flight and returned the fumble 23 yards for a touchdown that gave the Panthers a 35-28 lead they would not relinquish.
Patuxent was hoping to start the game quickly and give their freshman quarterback some early confidence, but the Sentinels foiled that plan from the outset.
Watson had his second pass attempt intercepted by Ahmad Saunders and five plays later the Sentinels were on the board first on a 27-yard run by Braelyn Younger.
Patuxent answered immediately as Watson connected with Jones on a 40-yard touchdown strike to bring the Panthers even at 7-7. But the Sentinels dominated the remainder of the first quarter, getting a 41-yard touchdown pass from House to Powell-Morris then Younger capped the opening frame with a 14-yard run that gave Fort Hill a 21-7 lead which the Sentinels extended to 28-7 in the second quarter.
Patuxent had been hurt by big plays in the first half, but its defense eliminated those in the second half and the Panthers’ offense reversed the outcome by forging several of their own. Watson connected with Johnson on a 79-yard strike and Jones on a 40-yarder then Dixon completed the improbable rally with his fumble return for another score.
Jones was named the Military Bowl Touchdown Club High School Football Player of the Week.

texts.0: Rise and Reclaim is alive and well in Cumberland, Maryland, as the Fort Hillfootballteam continued its redemption tour with a heart-stopping 43-42 victory over Bridgeport (W.Va.) on Friday.
texts.1:
## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
The game featured four touchdowns in the final 7:36, a successful two-point conversion in the closing minute, and a missed field goal on the final play in one of the most dramatic finishes this season.
The victory marked the second straight week Fort Hill avenged a 2025 loss as it continues its quest to reclaim its position as the state’s top 1A program. Fort Hill won four straight state championships before falling in last year’s state final, prompting the “Rise and Reclaim” motto for 2026. Fort Hill took a big step in that direction last week with a 35-21 victory over Hollidaysburg (Pa.). But Bridgeport was a different kind of monster.
Last year, Bridgeport handed Fort Hill a 49-14 thrashing in West Virginia, Fort Hill’s most lopsided regular-season loss since 2012. Friday’s rematch at Greenway Avenue Stadium carried historical significance, marking Bridgeport’s first game outside West Virginia after 1,098 consecutive in-state contests dating to 1921. The Sentinels again found themselves in trouble Friday, falling behind 21-7 before Bridgeport scored on a 70-yard play in the closing seconds of the second quarter to take a 28-14 halftime lead.
Fort Hill rallied to tie the game at 28 in the third quarter, setting up a wild finish.
Bridgeport took a 35-28 lead with 7:36 remaining, but Brady O’Neal answered 62 seconds later with a 78-yard touchdown pass to Carson Bender. Bridgeport again surged ahead, 42-35, before a three-minute Fort Hill drive was capped by Neek Taylor’s 7-yard scoring run, making it 42-41. There was no hesitation about going for two.
“When we started the next drive [down 42-35], everyone knew we’d be going for two,” Fort Hill coach Zach Alkire said.
After Bridgeport burned a timeout, Fort Hill called a quick pitch to the left. The wing got just enough of a block to give Taylor the room he needed to barely cross the goal line, putting Fort Hill ahead 43-42 with 51 seconds remaining.
texts.2:
## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
Bridgeport quickly moved into field-goal range, aided by a defensive pass-interference penalty. An encroachment penalty moved the final attempt from 44 to 39 yards, but the kick had the distance and sailed just wide right, sending Fort Hill to 5-0.
“The sideline went nuts,” Alkire said. “Kids running off the field, hugging. There was a lot of excitement, and we needed that.”
texts.3:
## **100 Wins, 46 Years in the Making**
Washington defeated Nandua (Va.), 20-10, in a contest that could easily be overlooked among the more than 100 games played by Maryland high schools this past weekend.
For Washington, however, it was anything but ordinary. The victory marked the program’s 100th varsity win — a milestone 46 years in the making.
Washington launched its first varsity football team in 1980 and lost its debut 42-0 to James M. Bennett. That proved to be a sign of things to come.
Except for the COVID-19 pandemic season in 2020, Washington has put a varsity team on the field every year since 1980. During that time, Washington has had only two winning seasons: 7-4 in 1989 and 8-5 in 2003. Yet the program has persevered despite finishing at or near the bottom of the Bayside standings for much of its history.
Perhaps the times are changing for this tiny school, which has about 600 students in grades 8-12.
Alec Meintzer inherited the program in 2023 while it was mired in an 18-game losing streak. That streak eventually reached 38 games before Washington broke through with a 16-6 victory over North East-Cecil last season. The win sparked something bigger: Washington finished 5-5, its first non-losing season since 2003.
Meintzer stepped down after the season, and Tremont White has taken over. This year’s team is officially 2-2, as the MPSSAA ruled that a scheduled season opener at Northampton (Va.) was a no-contest since the game was not played.
Now Washington has a chance to reach 3-2 for the first time since 1998 when it faces Arcadia (Va.) on Friday. The Jaguars defeated Arcadia, 36-16, last season.
texts.4:
## **Forfeits, No-Contests Becoming an Unwanted Trend**
The Maryland high school football season has reached the halfway point, and an unusual number of games have disappeared from the schedule because of forfeits, no-contests, or teams dropping games altogether.
The latest came this past weekend in Prince George’s County. According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line after the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests. The two teams will also play their remaining games this season on Saturdays.
According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line following the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests.
It is the latest in a growing list of unusual circumstances that have taken games off the schedule this season.
North Point and Westlake forfeited their season openers in Charles County because of what was termed out-of-season contact violations. Maryland School for the Deaf received a forfeit victory when its scheduled opponent disbanded the week of the game. Annapolis Area Christian has forfeited two games because of a lack of healthy players.
Weather has also played a role. Northampton (Va.) canceled its scheduled game at Washington because of what was described as “extreme heat,” while weather-related no-contests cost Flowers and Wise games from their schedules.
The situation has been particularly interesting at Edmondson-Westside. Through five weeks, the team has played only two games. One scheduled game was a forfeit, and two others were never played after Hancock and Benjamin Franklin dropped their football programs before the season.
This past weekend, Sidwell Friends, which rejoined the Mid-Atlantic Conference this season, forfeited its league opener at St. James on Saturday, citing not enough healthy players.
Meanwhile, Central Maryland Christian, down to 18 players, has reduced its regular-season schedule to four games.
While the reasons are varied, the result is the same: fewer opportunities for players to compete and an increasingly unpredictable high school football schedule.
texts.5:
## **Crofton Remains Unbeaten**
Crofton was featured early this season after what was then considered an upset victory over Old Mill.
Now, the Wildcats have established themselves as the team to beat in Anne Arundel County. Crofton is the county’s lone 5-0 team and one of just 21 undefeated teams remaining in the MPSSAA.
Dominic Jackson delivered the latest heroics, scoring on a 3-yard run to lift Crofton to a 20-17 overtime victory over Chesapeake-AA.
The teams tied at 14 after regulation. Gary Windsor gave Chesapeake-AA a 17-14 lead in the first overtime with a 27-yard field goal, but Crofton answered with a touchdown to complete the comeback and remain unbeaten.
texts.6:
## **Got Your Number**
Northwestern-PG edged Bladensburg, 22-20, over the weekend, marking the third consecutive year the Wildcats have beaten the Mustangs.
While the streak is notable, it is even more remarkable that Bladensburg is the only team Northwestern-PG has beaten since 2019.
Since midseason 2019, Northwestern-PG is 4-2 against Bladensburg but 0-53 against all other opponents. The Wildcats’ last victory over anyone other than Bladensburg came on Oct. 12, 2019, when Northwestern-PG thrashed DuVal, 47-6.

# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
The Sentinels, who wrapped up the top seed in the Class 1A West Region playoffs with last week's 49-14 thrashing over Smithsburg, haven't played at Greenway since Oct. 2.
Since their come-from-behind, 43-42 win over West Virginia power Bridgeport, the Sentinels have played at Mountain Ridge, North Hagerstown and Smithsburg.
Senior running back/linebacker Carson Bender admitted that the Sentinels had played a bit out of their element the past two weeks and a return to Greenway for Homecoming will be welcomed.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
"It's definitely mental stuff," Bender said after the win over Smithsburg. "We gotta be able to keep our cool. You know, Washington County being there for two weeks now, obviously the penalties ramped up there.
"We gotta clean it up. I think being back at home and being in our element next week and throughout the playoffs, that'll help us out a lot."
No. 1 Fort Hill (8-0) and No. 4 Allegany (5-3) will meet for the 106th time. The Sentinels have won 22 straight over the Campers and lead the all-time series 69-32-4.
Fort Hill won last year's game 57-13, setting records for the largest margin of victory and most points in series history.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Braelyn Younger also rushed for a record 203 yards and equalled the all-time touchdown mark with five scores.
"They're playing each other sometimes since five or six years old up through the Pop Warner stages and JV levels," Fort Hill coach Zack Alkire said. "There's lots of familiarity between the kids and what each team can do.
"Both sides look forward to it, both players and coaches, and this year's no different. It's obviously one of the games we circle on the calendar. The kids are pretty amped up for it."
Sophomore Levi House will make his third consecutive start at quarterback in place of Brady O'Neal.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
texts.3:
# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
House moved over to signal-caller from the tight end spot starting with the North Hagerstown game. In that game, House threw just one incompletion as the Sentinels ran for 369 yards.
But in last week's matchup with Smithsburg, the Sentinels weren't able to pop off as many explosive runs, forcing House to resort to his arm more often.
House gave the Leopards' defense fits all night, completing 7 of 10 passes for 110 yards while adding 60 yards with his feet.
"He completed a lot of those passes," Alkire said. "He made a lot of good decisions. He made a couple other decisions to run the ball instead of throwing the ball. So (we're) really happy with Levi's progress at the quarterback position and look forward to seeing how he can open things up a little bit on Saturday."
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
The Sentinels still grounded 269 yards on the Leopards. Fort Hill's longest run was a 45-yard touchdown by Channing Logsdon in the first quarter. Its second-biggest run was a 20-yarder by House.
Ground yards won't be easy to come by against an Allegany team that's given up an average of 15.2 points during its five-game win streak.
Bender leads the Sentinels with 879 yards rushing and has 13 touchdowns. He also led the team with 96 yards last week.
Neek Taylor has contributed 730 yards and 15 touchdowns. Logsdon (345 yards) and Isaiah Welsh (262 yards) have also been vital parts of Fort Hill's ground game.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Defensively, Fort Hill has allowed just 98 points overall for an average of 12.3 per game.
"We gotta come off the football first and foremost," Alkire said. "Our offensive line needs to be able to track people off the ball without holding and blocking in the back. We need to cut down on the penalties from the previous two weeks and hold onto the football.
texts.4:
# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
"We're gonna have to play really aggressive defense. We're gonna have to defend the pass when needed to, get pressure on the quarterback, make sure all of our gaps are filled and be aggressive running towards the football."
Since there are only seven teams in the West Region, Fort Hill will receive a first-round bye.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
As it stands now, Allegany is the No. 4 seed and will meet No. 5 Southern in the quarterfinals.
A Campers win in that game would set up a rematch between the city rivals in the region semifinals.
Fort Hill and Allegany played once last season, but met twice in 2024. The Sentinels won both games by an 87-0 margin on their way to an 11th state title.
"Homecoming's an important game for the community for both sides," Alkire said. "It's a game that you obviously wanna win. But the reality of it is that the playoffs are coming and a win would really give you a lot of momentum going into the playoffs."

# Patuxent wins 1A football championship
But that advantage was long forgotten in the waning seconds of the fourth quarter as the Panthers rallied for an improbable 35-28 victory to end the Sentinels’ four-year reign as 1A state champions.
“That was the greatest game that I’ve ever been a part of,” Patuxent coach Steve Crounse said after the Panthers recorded their second straight state title and third overall. “This group of young teenagers has so much resiliency. When we got that touchdown right before halftime, you could just feel their confidence growing.”
Fort Hill (9-4) owned a 21-7 lead at the end of the first quarter and then pushed the advantage to 28-7 with 2:23 remaining in the first half when quarterback Noah House connected with James Powell-Morris on a 47-yard touchdown strike on the Sentinels’ only play of that possession. Faced with a daunting task against the four-time reigning champs, Patuxent countered with a pivotal late score before the intermission.
Patuxent closed out the first half by marching 55 yards in nine plays, primarily on runs from Evan Jones. Then on the final play of the first half, Watson connected with Coen Boorstein on a 24-yard touchdown strike that trimmed the Sentinels’ lead to 28-14 heading into the locker room. But what was once a comfortable advantage would evaporate over the next 12 minutes.
“I just saw Coen make a good break on the ball and got it out to him and he brought it in,” Watson said. “I know last year they had a lot of seniors, but we just came in and believed in each other and our coaches.”
Fort Hill opened the third quarter with a methodical, 12-play drive that lasted over six minutes but failed to yield any points and that served to bolster the Panthers’ resolve. On its second play of the second half, Watson connected with Peyton Johnson on a 79-yard scoring strike to trim the gap to 28-21, then Jones brought the Panthers even on a 38-yard run.
texts.14:
# Patuxent wins 1A football championship
In a game initially highlighted by big offensive plays, it was the Panthers’ defense that provided the biggest one of all. On the Sentinels’ ensuing possession, Patuxent’s John Edwards sacked House and jarred the ball loose from the Fort Hill quarterback and Jahkiye Dixon snared the ball in flight and returned the fumble 23 yards for a touchdown that gave the Panthers a 35-28 lead they would not relinquish.
Patuxent was hoping to start the game quickly and give their freshman quarterback some early confidence, but the Sentinels foiled that plan from the outset.
Watson had his second pass attempt intercepted by Ahmad Saunders and five plays later the Sentinels were on the board first on a 27-yard run by Braelyn Younger.
Patuxent answered immediately as Watson connected with Jones on a 40-yard touchdown strike to bring the Panthers even at 7-7. But the Sentinels dominated the remainder of the first quarter, getting a 41-yard touchdown pass from House to Powell-Morris then Younger capped the opening frame with a 14-yard run that gave Fort Hill a 21-7 lead which the Sentinels extended to 28-7 in the second quarter.
Patuxent had been hurt by big plays in the first half, but its defense eliminated those in the second half and the Panthers’ offense reversed the outcome by forging several of their own. Watson connected with Johnson on a 79-yard strike and Jones on a 40-yarder then Dixon completed the improbable rally with his fumble return for another score.
Jones was named the Military Bowl Touchdown Club High School Football Player of the Week.

Rise and Reclaim is alive and well in Cumberland, Maryland, as the Fort Hillfootballteam continued its redemption tour with a heart-stopping 43-42 victory over Bridgeport (W.Va.) on Friday.

## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
The game featured four touchdowns in the final 7:36, a successful two-point conversion in the closing minute, and a missed field goal on the final play in one of the most dramatic finishes this season.
The victory marked the second straight week Fort Hill avenged a 2025 loss as it continues its quest to reclaim its position as the state’s top 1A program. Fort Hill won four straight state championships before falling in last year’s state final, prompting the “Rise and Reclaim” motto for 2026. Fort Hill took a big step in that direction last week with a 35-21 victory over Hollidaysburg (Pa.). But Bridgeport was a different kind of monster.
Last year, Bridgeport handed Fort Hill a 49-14 thrashing in West Virginia, Fort Hill’s most lopsided regular-season loss since 2012. Friday’s rematch at Greenway Avenue Stadium carried historical significance, marking Bridgeport’s first game outside West Virginia after 1,098 consecutive in-state contests dating to 1921. The Sentinels again found themselves in trouble Friday, falling behind 21-7 before Bridgeport scored on a 70-yard play in the closing seconds of the second quarter to take a 28-14 halftime lead.
Fort Hill rallied to tie the game at 28 in the third quarter, setting up a wild finish.
Bridgeport took a 35-28 lead with 7:36 remaining, but Brady O’Neal answered 62 seconds later with a 78-yard touchdown pass to Carson Bender. Bridgeport again surged ahead, 42-35, before a three-minute Fort Hill drive was capped by Neek Taylor’s 7-yard scoring run, making it 42-41. There was no hesitation about going for two.
“When we started the next drive [down 42-35], everyone knew we’d be going for two,” Fort Hill coach Zach Alkire said.
After Bridgeport burned a timeout, Fort Hill called a quick pitch to the left. The wing got just enough of a block to give Taylor the room he needed to barely cross the goal line, putting Fort Hill ahead 43-42 with 51 seconds remaining.

## **Four Touchdowns in Less Than 8 Minutes**
Bridgeport quickly moved into field-goal range, aided by a defensive pass-interference penalty. An encroachment penalty moved the final attempt from 44 to 39 yards, but the kick had the distance and sailed just wide right, sending Fort Hill to 5-0.
“The sideline went nuts,” Alkire said. “Kids running off the field, hugging. There was a lot of excitement, and we needed that.”

## **100 Wins, 46 Years in the Making**
Washington defeated Nandua (Va.), 20-10, in a contest that could easily be overlooked among the more than 100 games played by Maryland high schools this past weekend.
For Washington, however, it was anything but ordinary. The victory marked the program’s 100th varsity win — a milestone 46 years in the making.
Washington launched its first varsity football team in 1980 and lost its debut 42-0 to James M. Bennett. That proved to be a sign of things to come.
Except for the COVID-19 pandemic season in 2020, Washington has put a varsity team on the field every year since 1980. During that time, Washington has had only two winning seasons: 7-4 in 1989 and 8-5 in 2003. Yet the program has persevered despite finishing at or near the bottom of the Bayside standings for much of its history.
Perhaps the times are changing for this tiny school, which has about 600 students in grades 8-12.
Alec Meintzer inherited the program in 2023 while it was mired in an 18-game losing streak. That streak eventually reached 38 games before Washington broke through with a 16-6 victory over North East-Cecil last season. The win sparked something bigger: Washington finished 5-5, its first non-losing season since 2003.
Meintzer stepped down after the season, and Tremont White has taken over. This year’s team is officially 2-2, as the MPSSAA ruled that a scheduled season opener at Northampton (Va.) was a no-contest since the game was not played.
Now Washington has a chance to reach 3-2 for the first time since 1998 when it faces Arcadia (Va.) on Friday. The Jaguars defeated Arcadia, 36-16, last season.

## **Forfeits, No-Contests Becoming an Unwanted Trend**
The Maryland high school football season has reached the halfway point, and an unusual number of games have disappeared from the schedule because of forfeits, no-contests, or teams dropping games altogether.
The latest came this past weekend in Prince George’s County. According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line after the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests. The two teams will also play their remaining games this season on Saturdays.
According to one of the head coaches, an altercation in the handshake line following the Oxon Hill-Potomac game in Week 4 resulted in both teams forfeiting their Week 5 contests.
It is the latest in a growing list of unusual circumstances that have taken games off the schedule this season.
North Point and Westlake forfeited their season openers in Charles County because of what was termed out-of-season contact violations. Maryland School for the Deaf received a forfeit victory when its scheduled opponent disbanded the week of the game. Annapolis Area Christian has forfeited two games because of a lack of healthy players.
Weather has also played a role. Northampton (Va.) canceled its scheduled game at Washington because of what was described as “extreme heat,” while weather-related no-contests cost Flowers and Wise games from their schedules.
The situation has been particularly interesting at Edmondson-Westside. Through five weeks, the team has played only two games. One scheduled game was a forfeit, and two others were never played after Hancock and Benjamin Franklin dropped their football programs before the season.
This past weekend, Sidwell Friends, which rejoined the Mid-Atlantic Conference this season, forfeited its league opener at St. James on Saturday, citing not enough healthy players.
Meanwhile, Central Maryland Christian, down to 18 players, has reduced its regular-season schedule to four games.
While the reasons are varied, the result is the same: fewer opportunities for players to compete and an increasingly unpredictable high school football schedule.

## **Crofton Remains Unbeaten**
Crofton was featured early this season after what was then considered an upset victory over Old Mill.
Now, the Wildcats have established themselves as the team to beat in Anne Arundel County. Crofton is the county’s lone 5-0 team and one of just 21 undefeated teams remaining in the MPSSAA.
Dominic Jackson delivered the latest heroics, scoring on a 3-yard run to lift Crofton to a 20-17 overtime victory over Chesapeake-AA.
The teams tied at 14 after regulation. Gary Windsor gave Chesapeake-AA a 17-14 lead in the first overtime with a 27-yard field goal, but Crofton answered with a touchdown to complete the comeback and remain unbeaten.

## **Got Your Number**
Northwestern-PG edged Bladensburg, 22-20, over the weekend, marking the third consecutive year the Wildcats have beaten the Mustangs.
While the streak is notable, it is even more remarkable that Bladensburg is the only team Northwestern-PG has beaten since 2019.
Since midseason 2019, Northwestern-PG is 4-2 against Bladensburg but 0-53 against all other opponents. The Wildcats’ last victory over anyone other than Bladensburg came on Oct. 12, 2019, when Northwestern-PG thrashed DuVal, 47-6.

# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
The Sentinels, who wrapped up the top seed in the Class 1A West Region playoffs with last week's 49-14 thrashing over Smithsburg, haven't played at Greenway since Oct. 2.
Since their come-from-behind, 43-42 win over West Virginia power Bridgeport, the Sentinels have played at Mountain Ridge, North Hagerstown and Smithsburg.
Senior running back/linebacker Carson Bender admitted that the Sentinels had played a bit out of their element the past two weeks and a return to Greenway for Homecoming will be welcomed.

Advertisement
Advertisement
"It's definitely mental stuff," Bender said after the win over Smithsburg. "We gotta be able to keep our cool. You know, Washington County being there for two weeks now, obviously the penalties ramped up there.
"We gotta clean it up. I think being back at home and being in our element next week and throughout the playoffs, that'll help us out a lot."
No. 1 Fort Hill (8-0) and No. 4 Allegany (5-3) will meet for the 106th time. The Sentinels have won 22 straight over the Campers and lead the all-time series 69-32-4.
Fort Hill won last year's game 57-13, setting records for the largest margin of victory and most points in series history.

Advertisement
Braelyn Younger also rushed for a record 203 yards and equalled the all-time touchdown mark with five scores.
"They're playing each other sometimes since five or six years old up through the Pop Warner stages and JV levels," Fort Hill coach Zack Alkire said. "There's lots of familiarity between the kids and what each team can do.
"Both sides look forward to it, both players and coaches, and this year's no different. It's obviously one of the games we circle on the calendar. The kids are pretty amped up for it."
Sophomore Levi House will make his third consecutive start at quarterback in place of Brady O'Neal.

Advertisement

# Fort Hill seeks 23rd straight win over Allegany
House moved over to signal-caller from the tight end spot starting with the North Hagerstown game. In that game, House threw just one incompletion as the Sentinels ran for 369 yards.
But in last week's matchup with Smithsburg, the Sentinels weren't able to pop off as many explosive runs, forcing House to resort to his arm more often.
House gave the Leopards' defense fits all night, completing 7 of 10 passes for 110 yards while adding 60 yards with his feet.
"He completed a lot of those passes," Alkire said. "He made a lot of good decisions. He made a couple other decisions to run the ball instead of throwing the ball. So (we're) really happy with Levi's progress at the quarterback position and look forward to seeing how he can open things up a little bit on Saturday."

Bender leads the Sentinels with 879 yards rushing and has 13 touchdowns. He also led the team with 96 yards last week.

"We gotta come off the football first and foremost," Alkire said. "Our offensive line needs to be able to track people off the ball without holding and blocking in the back. We need to cut down on the penalties from the previous two weeks and hold onto the football.

"We're gonna have to play really aggressive defense. We're gonna have to defend the pass when needed to, get pressure on the quarterback, make sure all of our gaps are filled and be aggressive running towards the football."
Since there are only seven teams in the West Region, Fort Hill will receive a first-round bye.

"Homecoming's an important game for the community for both sides," Alkire said. "It's a game that you obviously wanna win. But the reality of it is that the playoffs are coming and a win would really give you a lot of momentum going into the playoffs."
